bounded world-model artifacts. It owns the position, constitutional
intents and manifesto; the role split and the imported product-lineage
concepts with the Builder Project specialisation; what a world model is,

profile; the core claims; the units; the fourteen-stage flow; the
representation, materialisation, publication and attribute-ledger laws;
entity recovery and the entity cut construction law; the Markov-object
overlay construction law; the saturation, composition and projection
laws; the control and data planes; the proof law; world-model-driven
development; the output; the companion surfaces; and this profile's
refinements of the core result algebra.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises hold where world-model work is done under this
profile; they are adopted with it and do not follow from the foundations
(P1, P6):

- I1: institutional source systems enact domain function and stay
  sovereign for operational truth; the builder observes them and replaces

- I2: records do not carry their own meaning, and the people who work with
  them already commit to the objects, implicitly in code paths, records
  and workflows, or explicitly in schemas and policy;
- I3: probabilistic systems can propose correspondences across domains,
  and delivery at volume needs deterministic execution;
- I4: some builders work over a representation space in which identity is

concepts.definition: Assurance is the governed basis for accepting a traced source observation as a qualified semantic claim. The Attribute Ledger is an append-only ordered record of qualified claims over stable object identity, potentially including observed/derived values, interpretations, rules, relations, provenance, authority and effective/observed/publication coordinates.

grounding.quote:
| Assurance | the governed basis on which a traced source observation is accepted as a qualified semantic claim; it answers why a claim is lawful world-model truth rather than merely a raw observation | P6 |
| Attribute Ledger | an append-only ordered record of qualified attribute claims over a stable object identity; entries may carry observed values, derived values, interpreted meanings, rule or constraint claims, topology or relation claims, provenance and authority claims, and effective, observed and publication coordinates | P4b, P3 |

concepts.label: Attribute Ledger and Assurance

concepts.definition: An Entity Cut is the primary published semantic unit: an identity-bearing, bounded, evidence-backed immutable selection projected from the attribute ledger. Its eight surfaces are identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity, each traced to ledger entries and assurance. It is lawful without an identity direction.

grounding.quote:
Entity Cut. The primary published semantic unit: an identity-bearing,
bounded, evidence-backed cut of a recovered entity, projected from the
attribute ledger (P3, P6; rc.2 #entity-cut). An entity cut is lawful
without an identity direction. It publishes identity, boundary,
authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity, each
traced to ledger entries and their assurance basis. Builder projects may
begin with looser object candidates; world-model publication converges
them into entity cuts, or explicitly leaves them as non-object artifacts
such as treatment surfaces, covariance edges or temporal reference
artifacts (P3, P5).

concepts.label: Entity Cut

concepts.definition: A Markov object is the candidate theoretical construct of a stable self-bounding pattern whose internal state is reasoned about through an effective blanket. The substrate-neutral working claim expects this topology across biological systems, natural-language traces, learned representations and institutional systems. It accounts for recovery of already committed objects rather than their invention.

grounding.quote:
A Markov object is
a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure whose internal
state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket. The term is
substrate-neutral: the same topology is expected wherever a constraint
structure admits stable configurations, in biological systems (Friston's
original setting), in the natural-language traces those systems emit, in
learned representations built over those traces (LLMs), and in the
engineered institutional systems descended from both. The working claim
is that world-model construction is possible because this topology
propagates across substrates: what domain experts recognise as "objects"
in an institutional system is the same kind of structure Friston
described for biological systems, re-expressed through another
substrate. The profile is the practice of making that structure explicit,
traceable and publishable (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Candidate Markov-object construct

conditions: The geometric reading is situated in a representation space.
concepts.definition: An effective blanket is a low-rank projection along which identity survives treatment. Attribute bases provide distributed evidence, not a crisp column-membership boundary: firing attributes align only partially with identity, and overwriting apparent nonmembers can transfer identity.
concepts.label: Effective blanket

conditions: A declared representation space exists.
concepts.definition: A Markov-Object Overlay is an optional geometric package attached to an entity cut, adding identity direction, projection support, distributed evidence and effective coordinate. It is a candidate-class overlay of a candidate construct even when its direction is verified for publication; its absence does not weaken a lawful entity cut.

grounding.quote: | Markov-Object Overlay | an optional geometric overlay on an entity cut, admissible only where a declared representation space exists; it adds an identity direction, projection support and effective coordinate, constructed and verified under §10; the overlay strengthens an entity cut, and its absence does not weaken one | P3, P6 |

This status attaches to the construct and to overlays built on it. A
published Markov-object overlay is a candidate-class overlay of a
candidate construct, not a certified blanket of a formally established
object. It does not attach to entity cuts: an entity cut is lawful
published truth on its own admissibility test (§9) and does not inherit
the construct's candidate status. A candidate entity that has not met
that test is a candidate; a published entity cut is not (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Markov-Object Overlay

concepts.definition: A Treatment Surface reinterprets meaning from one domain into another; a Covariance Edge declares how changes in one object correspond to changes in another; an Adjoint Mapping is the interpret-back contract for a treatment; a Temporal Reference Artifact is a changing value list, code set or classification whose semantics affect interpretation.

grounding.quote:
| Treatment Surface | a semantic reinterpretation from one domain into another | P1 |
| Covariance Edge | a declared relation showing how changes in one object correspond to changes in another | P1, P3 |
| Adjoint Mapping | the interpret-back contract for a treatment | P1 |
| Temporal Reference Artifact | a changing value list, code set or classification set whose semantics matter for object interpretation | P3, P1 |

concepts.label: Treatment, covariance, adjoint and temporal-reference units

concepts.definition: A Composed World Model references and stitches published domain artifacts while preserving identity, version and local authority. A Projection is a downstream or user-facing artifact derived from the semantic kernel. A Query Plane optionally serves query/traversal without becoming publication authority.

grounding.quote:
| Composed World Model | a higher-order world model built by referencing and stitching published domain artifacts while preserving their identity, version and local authority | P4a, P6 |
| Projection | a user-facing or downstream-facing artifact derived from the semantic kernel | P1 |
| Query Plane | an optional downstream serving surface that makes published domain artifacts or composed world models queryable or traversable without becoming the constitutional publication authority | P6 |

concepts.label: Composed World Model, Projection and Query Plane

concepts.definition: The published semantic layer is the single constitutional truth surface for world-model meaning: published domain artifacts, bounded fragments/entity cuts, treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings, temporal reference artifacts and composed models built by reference. Epistemic overlays, query planes, mapping reports and compiled execution artifacts are downstream or supporting.

grounding.quote:
World-model work has one constitutional truth surface: the published
semantic layer (P6; rc.2 #single-truth-surface). That layer consists of
published domain artifacts; their bounded fragments and published entity
cuts; explicit treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings and
temporal reference artifacts; and composed world models built by
reference from those published artifacts. Everything else is downstream
or supporting: epistemic overlays, query planes, mapping reports and
compiled deterministic execution artifacts. Those surfaces may be
important; they do not create a second truth surface (P6, P1).

concepts.label: Published semantic layer

concepts.definition: Epistemic overlays hold probabilistic correspondence candidates, confidence/ranking, ambiguities, anomaly/surprise and candidate mappings/treatments. They are distinct from accepted semantic treatments, published artifacts and compiled deterministic execution.

grounding.quote:
That overlay may
include correspondence candidates; confidence and ranking; ambiguity
registers; anomaly and surprise signals; and candidate mappings or
treatment suggestions. The overlay is useful because it lets
probabilistic reasoning operate over a governed semantic substrate rather
than over detached strings, schemas or raw tables. But the overlay is not
the same thing as published semantic truth: accepted semantic treatments,
published domain artifacts and compiled deterministic execution artifacts
remain distinct from probabilistic overlays (P6, P0).

concepts.label: Epistemic overlay

concepts.definition: The fourteen-stage source-defined construction flow is Observe, Trace, Extract, Assure, Ledger, Bound, Materialise, Relate, Publish, Compose, optionally Align, Project, optionally Compile, and optionally Serve/query. It describes operations; this interpretation does not perform them.

grounding.quote:
The profile proceeds through these stages (P4b, P6; rc.2 #method-flow and
the stage anchors named in §15):

1. Observe. Gather source evidence from the strongest available surfaces
   (§3 Evidence hierarchy): runtime behaviour; source records and events;
   code and configuration when available; interfaces and schemas; docs and
   metadata.

concepts.label: World-model construction flow

concepts.definition: The publication ledger records immutable published domain-artifact cuts and object projections; the attribute ledger records qualified semantic claims over object identity. In the initial lane Git and filesystem suffice for publication, while a later database is a query-plane complement.

grounding.quote:
The
filesystem and Git are sufficient for the publication plane in the
initial lane. A database, if introduced later, is a query-plane
complement rather than the constitutional publication authority. In other
words: Git is the publication ledger; a database is the query plane
(P6). This publication ledger is distinct from the attribute ledger: the
attribute ledger records qualified semantic claims over object identity,
and the publication ledger records immutable published cuts of domain
artifacts and object projections. Both should remain append-only and
replayable (P4b).

concepts.label: Publication ledger

conditions: The overlay law applies in a declared representation space where identity is geometric.
concepts.definition: An identity direction is a low-rank geometric combination over attribute columns, canonically d(object) = μ(evidence_object) − μ(evidence_null) across contexts. A null peer is structurally similar but lacks the candidate's identity content.

grounding.quote:
Derive the identity axis as a low-rank projection over the paired
evidence (P3, P1; rc.2 #2-identity-direction-extraction). The canonical
form is the mean offset

`d(object) = μ(evidence_object) − μ(evidence_null)`

concepts.label: Identity direction and null peer

conditions: The candidate appears in multiple contexts.
concepts.definition: Invariant core is evidence whose contribution to the identity direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts; context coat is evidence selected by a specific context and carrying reinterpretation. Both are evidence: core carries identity, coat treatment. Their ratio characterises rather than measures quality.

grounding.quote:
For candidates that appear in multiple contexts, decompose the attribute
evidence into an invariant core, the attributes whose contribution to the
identity direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts, and a context
coat, the attributes selected by the specific context, carrying
contextual reinterpretation rather than identity per se (P3;
rc.2 #4-core-and-coat-decomposition). Both are evidence. The core carries
identity; the coat carries treatment. The coat to core ratio is a
characterisation, not a quality metric (P3, P1).

concepts.label: Invariant core and context coat

concepts.definition: Semantic control comprises published artifacts, composed models, treatment/covariance/adjoint relations and epistemic overlays. The high-volume data plane comprises deterministic executables compiled from accepted understanding. This division separates roles without creating a second semantic truth surface.

grounding.quote:
The semantic
control plane consists of published domain artifacts; composed world
models; treatments, covariance edges and adjoint mappings; and epistemic
overlays for correspondence, ranking and ambiguity. The high-volume data
plane consists of deterministic executable artifacts compiled from
accepted semantic understanding. That means: world-model artifacts carry
semantic truth; epistemic overlays carry probabilistic correspondence and
uncertainty; compiled execution artifacts carry deterministic runtime
behaviour. This is a plane split, not a truth split; the semantic truth
surface remains the published world-model layer (§3 Single truth
surface) (P6).

concepts.label: Semantic control plane and deterministic data plane

concepts.definition: Seven distinct world-model result refinements address cut admissibility, direction acceptance, overlay publication, overlay storage, null-peer discrimination, a promotion-gate run, and ledger saturation. Each maps a value to exactly one core value for its named predicate; construct standing and publication kind are separate categories.

grounding.quote:
| cut admissibility | is the entity cut admissible (§9 Admissibility) | the entity cut's eight surfaces are explicit, traceable and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence altitude proportional to its claim |
| direction acceptance | is a candidate identity direction accepted (§10 Identity-direction extraction, Verification by treatment) | the identity direction is built by an admissible extraction, projection along it preserves object identity under held-out treatments, and at least one acceptable verification is recorded |
| overlay publication | does a published overlay rest on an accepted direction (§8 Representation law, §10 Verification by treatment) | the published overlay's direction has a recorded acceptable verification |
| overlay storage | does the stored overlay keep its package (§10 Storage shape) | the stored overlay retains the six surfaces of §10 Storage shape |
| null-peer discrimination | is the candidate a lawful Markov object by null-peer comparison (§10 Null-peer discrimination) | the candidate passes the uniqueness test and the transfer test |
| promotion gate | does a run of the promotion gate meet its predicate (§4 Epistemic status) | this run of the direction-native conditional-independence test meets its predicate |
| saturation | is the attribute ledger sufficiently saturated for publication (§11 Saturation law) | materially important attributes have traceable support, the remaining gaps are explicit ambiguities, and the resulting cut is stable enough to publish |

conditions: Where the product publishes typed asset surfaces under its graph-execution carrier law and local design.
exceptions: If AssetSurface contracts are not published, apply the same binding law to the equivalent typed contract named by the design module.

grounding.quote:
- the surface's State is derived from AssetSurface projections, not from
  a UX-local re-declaration of the asset shape;
- its product-truth-changing Msg variants map one to one to AssetSurface
  action-registry entries, or wrap them through a documented projection
  with no hidden semantic change;
- UX-local Msg variants are reserved for view-local concerns (open or
  closed, sort order, filter input);
- selection within the surface emits a Context update, or equivalent,
  consistent with the product's selection contract;
- writes from the surface go through the AssetSurface action registry,
  not through direct file or service calls.

This is the rule that produces strong functional consistency between
front end and back end: the same typed contract is the ground truth on
both sides (P1, P3). If the product does not publish AssetSurface
contracts, the design module names the equivalent typed contract and
applies the same binding law to that contract. Absence of an admitted
contract blocks product-truth-changing UX actions (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Bind to one or more contracts as data sources/action targets. Derive State from projections without redeclaring asset shape. Product-truth Msg variants map one-to-one to action entries or documented projections with no hidden semantic change. Reserve local Msg for view concerns. Selection emits Context or equivalent consistent with the selection contract. Writes use the action registry, never direct file/service calls. The same typed contract grounds front and back ends. Missing admitted contracts block product-truth-changing actions.

conditions: Runtime ownership is stated for the graph-execution profile.

grounding.quote:
In the graph-execution profile the runtime owns continuation (PROFILES
§2) and the product is a cooperative bounded-step subsystem. The UX
twin: the view does not own state continuation (P0, P6;
rc.2 #8-ux-twin-of-odd-115a-view-does-not-own-continuation). State
transitions flow through declared Msg actions interpreted by the reducer.
A view does not:

- decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event;
- chain several state updates locally without emitting them as separate
  Msg values;
- carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures or module-level
  variables.

If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that machine
belongs in the reducer as part of State, with explicit Msg transitions
between phases; the view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is
in (P1). The discipline test is the Msg-replay test: can the view's
behaviour be replayed by replaying its Msg log against an empty State? If
the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view (P4b).

constraints.statement: Runtime owns continuation; the product is a cooperative bounded-step subsystem. The view neither decides next state independently, chains local updates without separate Msg values, nor retains hidden inter-event state in refs/closures/module variables. Multi-step machines belong in reducer State with explicit phase Msg transitions and a purely projected view. Failure to reproduce view behaviour by replaying its Msg log against empty State indicates leaked continuation.

conditions: Before claiming closure under this profile for any product UX surface.
exceptions: A pure projection-only surface may use the expressly permitted no-effect proof.

grounding.quote:
Every product UX surface carries at least one executable Msg-replay proof
for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming closure
under this profile (P4b, P6; rc.2 #8a-msg-replay-proof-requirement).

constraints.statement: Every product-meaningful interaction family needs at least one executable proof. Include initial State, ordered Msg log, expected final State, ordered expected Cmds, success/failure Msgs from Cmd interpretation, and deterministic injections for time/randomness/generated IDs/external payloads. Correctness depending on unrepresented DOM state; mutable refs/module variables/closures/timers/effect-handler memory; file/network results bypassing typed Msg; or local state changing behaviour after unmount/replay makes the proof fail.

exceptions: Out-of-render mutation is excepted only when part of the declared effect membrane, such as an imperative-interop platform handle already named in the design module.

grounding.quote:
Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function
component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived
expression or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision
recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function
signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body
(P1, P0). A view that depends on out-of-render mutation, for example a
ref written from inside an effect handler and read during render,
violates §6 unless the mutation is part of the declared effect membrane,
for example a platform handle for imperative interop already named in the
design module (P6).

constraints.statement: Preserve State → ViewTree and a side-effect-free body, typed inputs/output, explicitly consumed inputs, no mutable closure state across renders and no undeclared input reads. Record implementation shape as a stack decision. Out-of-render mutation ordinarily violates the effect-membrane rule.
constraints.uncertainty: The full §6 membrane law is not supplied.

conditions: Runtime validation applies at every untrusted or out-of-process seam.

grounding.quote:
UX-consumed types come from the shared front-end and back-end contract
(P3, P1; rc.2 #10-type-sharing-rule). A UX surface does not re-declare
back-end record shapes; it imports them from the shared contract module,
typically the same package or a dedicated `contracts/` package.

Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam
(P6; it makes DESIGN_MODULE §4's preference for parsing and admitting
foreign data once at ingress an obligation at these seams):

- HTTP or RPC responses;
- MCP payloads;
- file-loaded records;
- websocket or event-stream messages;
- agent or worker outputs;
- URL, storage, clipboard or browser integration payloads.

The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so that the same type
definition is the source of both compile-time types and runtime
validators; the mechanism choice is project-local. Compile-time
TypeScript alone is not sufficient at these seams (P6, P1). UX-local types
are allowed for view-local concerns: form input draft state, sort order
enums, filter strings. UX-local types do not shadow back-end types (P3).

constraints.statement: Import backend record shapes from shared contracts, typically the same or a contracts/ package; never redeclare/shadow them. Validate HTTP/RPC, MCP, file-loaded, websocket/event-stream, agent/worker and URL/storage/clipboard/browser-integration payloads at ingress. Use one typed-schema definition for compile-time types and runtime validators; TypeScript alone is insufficient. The schema mechanism is project-local; UX-local draft/sort/filter types are allowed only for view-local concerns.

conditions: The surface is the public face of a product capability.
exceptions: Accessibility is optional for internal-only debug surfaces when the design module records the exemption.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares
(P2, P6; rc.2 #11-accessibility-minimum):

- semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or
  platform-equivalent affordances);
- keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has
  a pointer interaction;
- focus management on dynamic content changes;
- accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks
  a native semantic equivalent;
- colour contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG
  AA is the recommended default for web).

Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional
for internal-only debug surfaces, and the design module records the
exemption (P2, P6). This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with
stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector
procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it
from their design modules (P2).

constraints.statement: Declare semantic structure/platform equivalents, keyboard/platform navigation for every pointer action, focus management for dynamic changes, annotations for custom interactive elements without native semantics, and contrast at the declared project standard. WCAG AA is a recommended web default, not a mandated universal standard. Stricter obligations require a project-local refinement cited from design modules.
constraints.uncertainty: Later sections recognise recorded exemptions more generally without supplying their full authorization criteria.

conditions: Product authority adopts the profile for a project.
exceptions: Scope may cover only selected UX surfaces if recorded.
constraints.statement: Record nine items: profile name; stack and justification; irreducible carrier set and required structural diagram; each surface's State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub before implementation; consumed/emitted contract bindings; effect mechanism and interpreted Cmd algebra; executable replay-proof surface; required accessibility refinement; explicit view/effect exemptions. Adoption is per project and recorded surface scope.
constraints.uncertainty: Relationship between limited adoption and default scaffold governance is not explicitly resolved here.

conditions: Any of: reachable from product shell; used as ticket/requirement/design/release/review proof; mutates product truth; spawns/attaches/resumes/dispatches work; changes Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence or provenance.
exceptions: Scaffold/prototype/debug/temporary-proof exemption only with the complete specified design-module or ticket record.
constraints.statement: Any listed trigger establishes default governance. Exemption records scope, permitted operations, forbidden or bounded mutation, visible user-facing scaffold/debug label, superseding authoritative surface, retirement condition/owning ticket and non-closure condition preventing release while scaffold remains. An exempt scaffold cannot accumulate into production: retire it, reprice it as governed UX, or keep it outside product closure.

conditions: During a short iteration window when per-change proof cost exceeds expected correction cost.

grounding.quote:
The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where
the debt is local to UX realisation and the governing method allows
follow-up. It may not close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden
state continuation or authority drift remain unclassified (P6, P4b).

Closure under this profile for a product UX surface still requires the
§8 Msg-replay proof and the §11 accessibility obligations unless an
explicit exemption is recorded. The sprint can defer those obligations
during iteration; it cannot erase them (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Non-escrowable findings must be recorded and exit through standalone repricing or sprint supersession; UX must not become a hidden constructive carrier. Close review examines every changed screen/state/product-meaningful interaction against cited authority and classifies each finding. Explicit paydown tickets permit sprint close only for local UX-realisation debt where the governing method allows follow-up. No close with unclassified carrier gaps, hidden continuation or authority drift. Surface closure still requires replay proof and accessibility unless explicitly exempted; deferral never erases obligations.
constraints.uncertainty: Generic escrow mechanics and four of the six close classifications depend on unsupplied TICKETS §3.

conditions: Continued iteration is more expensive or less trustworthy than review.
constraints.statement: The sprint should close. Nonexhaustive valid triggers are timebox expiry, too many changed states for casual review, stale screenshots/walkthroughs, behaviour change beyond polish, and reviewer uncertainty requiring reconciliation before safe further iteration.

conditions: Any one listed failure pattern holds.
exceptions: The listed membrane and recorded-exemption qualifications remain operative.

grounding.quote:
Any of these is a violation of this profile. Repeated violations are not
normalised by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced (P6,
P4b).

constraints.statement: Each of the seventeen grounded patterns independently violates the profile: direct render mutation; product state in local cells; transition decisions in effects; view state machines; render refs outside membrane; shadowed/redeclared backend types; direct file/network action writes; unrecorded view exemption; unexempted public accessibility omission; untyped reducer-bypassing two-way binding; imperative Cmd logic in effects; failed empty-State replay; unadmitted truth-changing message; unvalidated ingress; reachable/mutating/proof scaffold without record; local conventions weakening the profile; sprint closure with unclassified or unticketed deferred proof/accessibility/carrier/scaffold/authority debt. Repetition does not normalise violations: repair or reprice.
constraints.uncertainty: Pattern 7's literal AssetSurface wording is read alongside §7's expressly permitted equivalent typed contract, without inventing additional exceptions.

conditions: A surface review under this profile; the sprint question applies if a UX sprint was used.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface review under this profile should answer (P6, P2;
rc.2 #15-review-questions):

1. What is the surface's State, Msg and Update?
2. What is the surface's Cmd and Sub algebra?
3. Which AssetSurface or equivalent typed contracts does it bind to?
4. Which product-truth-changing messages map to admitted carriers?
5. Where is the effect membrane, and what Cmd values does it interpret?
6. Is `View = f(State)` provably pure for this surface?
7. Can the surface's behaviour be replayed from a Msg log (the Msg-replay
   proof of §8)?
8. Are all UX-consumed types imported from the shared contract?
9. Are all out-of-process payloads runtime-validated before entering UX
   state?
10. Are view-shape, effect-membrane, accessibility, scaffold or debug
    exemptions documented?
11. What realisation stack is chosen, and how does it preserve the §4 Elm
    process model?
12. Does the surface honour the §8 rule that the view does not own
    continuation under user replay?
13. Does the design module include the design profile's carrier set and
    structural carrier diagram required for closure (DESIGN_MODULE §6 and
    §7)?
14. If the work used a UX sprint, did close review classify every deferred
    proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold and authority finding?

If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete (P6,
P5).

constraints.statement: Review should answer all fourteen grounded questions concerning State/Msg/Update; Cmd/Sub; bindings; admitted messages; membrane/interpreted Cmds; purity; replay; shared types; validated ingress; documented exemptions; stack/Elm preservation; continuation; carrier set/diagram; and sprint classification of every deferred finding. Any unanswerable applicable question makes the design module incomplete. The recommendation to answer is distinct from §15's result basis condition.

conditions: A surface review is performed on its exact basis.
exceptions: While the competing compliance tests await owner ruling, apply the stricter §4–§10 test under the source's fail-closed rule.

grounding.quote:
| surface review | `compliant` | satisfied | §4 to §10 hold under inspection and no §13 failure pattern is present (§4 Realisation discretion), and every §14 review question is answered from the design module. The first part is the stricter of the two compliance tests of §4, which disagree: §4 Process model without stack mandate counts a realisation that preserves §4 to §8 as compliant. The choice between them is pending the product owner's ruling and is not settled by this mapping; while it is pending, this mapping applies the stricter test under the fail-closed rule of §1 Authority. The last part, every §14 review question answered from the design module, is in neither test: it is the basis condition that separates `compliant` from `design_module_incomplete` |
| surface review | `violation` | falsified | the test of `compliant` fails: a §13 failure pattern is present, a realisation that §4 Process model without stack mandate rejects is used, or a rule of §4 to §10 does not hold under inspection; the pattern, realisation or rule is the counterexample |
| surface review | `design_module_incomplete` | invalid_basis | no counterexample of `violation` is found, and a §14 review question cannot be answered from the design module, so the design module, on which the review rests, cannot support the evaluation; the value names the unanswered question |

constraints.statement: compliant→satisfied requires §4–§10 under inspection, no §13 pattern and every §14 answer from the design module. violation→falsified names a failure pattern, rejected realisation or failed §4–§10 rule as counterexample. design_module_incomplete→invalid_basis applies only if no violation counterexample is found and a review question cannot be answered from the design module; name that question. Missing answers alone are not the violation branch.
constraints.uncertainty: The owner has not resolved §4–§8 versus §4–§10 compliance; the mapping expressly does not settle it.

conditions: Each result applies only to its own named predicate; closure results apply where product-surface closure is claimed.
exceptions: A recorded exemption may cover a closure obligation; an open sprint does not claim closure and deferred obligations are escrow.

grounding.quote:
| replay proof | `replay_passes` | satisfied | the proof reproduces its expected final State and ordered Cmd values on its injected deterministic values, and no dependency that §8 lists decides its correctness |
| replay proof | `replay_fails` | falsified | the proof diverges from its expected final State or Cmd values, or its correctness depends on something §8 lists; the divergence or the dependency is the counterexample |
| closure obligations | `closure_obligations_met` | satisfied | every product-meaningful interaction family carries its Msg-replay proof and the surface its accessibility declarations, or a recorded exemption covers the obligation |
| closure obligations | `closure_unproven` | falsified | an interaction family lacks its proof or the surface an accessibility declaration, with no recorded exemption; that family or obligation is the counterexample. Inside an open UX sprint closure is not claimed, and a deferred obligation is escrow under §12 |
| carrier admission | `carrier_admitted` | satisfied | each product-truth-changing message or action maps to an admitted carrier of §3 and binds under §7 to an AssetSurface contract where the product publishes one, otherwise to the equivalent typed contract its design module names |
| carrier admission | `carrier_missing` | falsified | a product-truth-changing message or action has no admitted carrier or typed contract (§13 pattern 13); that message or action is the counterexample |

constraints.statement: replay_passes→satisfied iff expected final State and ordered Cmds reproduce with deterministic injections and no forbidden correctness dependency; replay_fails→falsified names divergence/dependency. closure_obligations_met→satisfied requires each meaningful family proof and accessibility declarations, or covering exemptions; closure_unproven→falsified names missing unexempted proof/declaration. carrier_admitted→satisfied requires every truth-changing message/action to map to an admitted carrier and applicable AssetSurface/equivalent binding; carrier_missing→falsified names the message/action lacking admission.

conditions: Fallback core values apply where no refined value applies.

grounding.quote:
Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value
directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):
`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,
naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim
needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and
`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground
other than `design_module_incomplete` (P5).

Fail closed (§1 Authority). Where this profile is ambiguous for a case,
the surface review applies the stricter interpretation and returns its
value under it; the ambiguity alone never yields `compliant`. Where the
ambiguity leaves a term the review depends on undefined, so that no
stricter interpretation is fixed, the review returns
`out_of_frame` and names the term and its owner
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or
indeterminate, first case). A reprice or a scoped exemption, the other
two exits of §1 Authority, is a re-entry or a scope recorded in the
design module, not a value of this section (P5, P6).

Blocked for want of a carrier (§3, §7). The surface's carrier admission
returns `carrier_missing`, and its review returns `violation` (§13 pattern
13), each for its own predicate. A construction step that needs the
missing carrier stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`, which
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
maps; the stop names the missing carrier, its owner in the product's
design and the re-entry, which is to author the carrier or to reprice the
requirement (P5, P6).

Two collisions are resolved here (P1): "blocked" for want of a carrier is
not the ambiguity outcome `blocked` of
[ACTIVATION §3 Ambiguity outcome](ACTIVATION.md#ambiguity-outcome), and
`design_module_incomplete` is not the value `incomplete` of ACTIVATION §3
Construction availability. An exempt scaffold is a recorded scope (§12),
not a result; evaluations outside its recorded scope proceed under this
section. The six close classifications of §12 belong to TICKETS §3 and are
not mapped here (P6).

constraints.statement: Fallback indeterminate names deciding evidence; out_of_frame identifies an undeclared needed relation/capability; invalid_basis covers unsupported basis other than design_module_incomplete. Ambiguity uses a fixed stricter interpretation, never automatically compliant; if an essential term remains undefined with no fixed stricter reading, return out_of_frame naming term/owner. Reprice/exemption are re-entry/scope, not results. Missing carrier yields carrier_missing and violation for separate predicates; a dependent construction step stops re_entry_requested(authority), naming carrier, design owner and author-carrier/reprice-requirement re-entry. This is not ACTIVATION's ambiguity blocked; design_module_incomplete is not construction incomplete. Scaffold scope is not a result; outside-scope evaluations proceed normally. TICKETS close classifications are not mapped here.
constraints.uncertainty: External construction-result mappings are not supplied.

Binding declared under PROFILES §1 (new; it makes
the member map's "entity-cut law consumed by FOUNDATIONS P3" an explicit
relation rather than a route): where FOUNDATIONS §2 defines an Object as
a subject with scoped identity, a boundary, current state and declared

the constitutional identity of this profile. Those concerns may later be

two core intents (P2, P3).

not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Do not present policy choices as derived or candidate constructs as established. Profile-owned choices include intents/manifesto/evidence order; entity-cut unit/eight ternary surfaces; initial Git publication lane; five treatment fields/preferred world-model→API→schema order; Builder Project narrowing; candidate construct/refinements/pin; mean-offset variants/exclusions/verification/publication/storage package; plane split; preferred mesh; proof wedge/spec-use boundary; and seven result refinements. Builder projects choose nonmandatory discrimination techniques; consumers choose carriers/layouts/schemas/storage topology. ACTIVATION owns treatment preservation/licensing/adequacy; FOUNDATIONS owns lineage; PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns relation carriers. The consumer map identifies: semantic-layer flow/materialisation/planes; cut units/refinements/discovery/materialisation/overlay/results; ledger immutability in Markov publication/overlay supersession; relations at flow stages 8/12; Builder specialisation at Units; candidate status in conformance/hypotheses/blanket/verification/results; geometric law in refinements/Units/materialisation/results; planes in alignment/compilation tooling; saturation/composition in sparse publication/flow/results. Proof policy and result returns have no separate named consumer. ODD/UX defer world semantics; glossary/output/inventory/disposition routes decide nothing. Every consumer is limited to its owner's rule.
constraints.uncertainty: External consumers and absent WORLD_MODEL §15 remain references, not inspected endpoints.

conditions: Under the selected complete method basis.
exceptions: A consuming Product may declare narrower Product-owned contexts without changing the profile's context.

grounding.quote:
SPEC_METHOD defines the general constitutional method for spec-driven
work; this profile is a domain-specific refinement of it for products
and projects that observe existing source systems and publish bounded
world-model artifacts (P6; rc.2 #method-role). The role split:
SPEC_METHOD defines the general process constitution; this profile
defines the constitutional refinement for world-model construction work,
including the current representation and publication law. Within the
world-model domain this profile is the primary method surface. It owns
the world-model bounded context `urn:stdo:bounded-context:world-model`
under the selected complete method basis. A consuming Product may declare
narrower Product-owned contexts without changing this profile's context by
proximity (P1, P6).

Where a product is both graph-native and world-model-driven, the
graph-execution profile (PROFILES §2) governs graph-native execution
shape, traversal law and product-authoring structure, and this profile
governs world-model semantics, publication and composition law. The two
compose; they do not compete (P6, P4a).

The meanings are adopted unchanged for this profile's scope under the
selected complete method basis. Their owner in FOUNDATIONS §2 is
retained, and a change to either context, any cited concept or taxonomy
clause, or the selected method basis invalidates the import until it is
reevaluated. The GLOSSARY only locates those source-owned meanings. No
other same-spelled concept is imported by this declaration. For each
import the source and target concept reference is the same listed
identity; the relation expands applicability into the target context and
mints no alias or new semantic owner (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: SPEC_METHOD owns general process; WORLD_MODEL owns the domain refinement and urn:stdo:bounded-context:world-model. For graph-native world-model products, ODD governs execution/traversal/product-authoring and WORLD_MODEL semantics/publication/composition. The four exact lineage identities import unchanged from recursive-product-taxonomy into world-model, with identical source/target concept references, retained FOUNDATIONS ownership, expanded applicability and no alias/new owner or same-spelled imports. Changes to either context, cited concept/taxonomy clause or selected basis invalidate imports until reevaluated; GLOSSARY only locates meanings.

conditions: World-model construction under the same selected complete method release containing source and target clauses.
exceptions: An installed builder Product may be substrate, but neither it nor its Install substitutes for the mutable Builder Project.

grounding.quote:

- semantic owners: FOUNDATIONS retains the source concept; this profile
