constraints.statement: The translation is Source Project→Builder Project only: no inverse, equivalence or universal claim that every Source Project qualifies. Exclude projects without the narrower configuration. Preserve source ownership and the target's distinct owner without authority over source taxonomy. This clause is the normative relation carrier. Any change to either concept/context, selected basis, builder configuration relation or governed scope invalidates translation until owning authorities reevaluate.

The model should expose real objects in context, coherent boundaries, relevant states/transitions, supporting evidence, governing value lists/classifications, adjacent reinterpretation, covariance and preservation/change/aggregation/delay/loss. It is not a replacement system of record, erasing central monolith, catalog entry, copied warehouse or schema registry substituted for comprehension.

conditions: These are intended objectives and capability recommendations, not findings about an actual model.
constraints.statement: Models should be bounded, inspectable, challengeable, evidenced, versioned, composable, projection-capable and machine-reasonable. Success should enable answers identifying a record's object/boundary/evidence/local authority, downstream meaning-changing treatment, relations of differently treated objects, historically governing values/classifications and explanation or nonexplanation of downstream figures from upstream reality.

conditions: Use the strongest available explanatory surfaces; code is conditional on availability.
exceptions: Code availability is never a prerequisite for comprehension.
constraints.statement: Prefer, in order, realised behaviour/emitted records or events; available code/rules/configuration; interfaces/schemas; large-scale observations; documentation/catalogs/operator testimony. Code is high-fidelity when available, while realised behaviour is broader for proprietary/partially visible/output-intelligible systems.

conditions: These four findings constrain the candidate construct and its overlays.
exceptions: They are not entity-cut admissibility conditions.

grounding.quote:
Four findings from the empirical program constrain how the profile treats
Markov objects. They are working refinements: the program has produced
candidate evidence for them, not a formal closure, and the profile adopts
them as the best current reading of the construct (P3, P6;
rc.2 #four-working-refinements-indicated-by-the-empirical-program). They
are stated in the order and sense the pinned companion surface carries
(§13 Companion surfaces), each with the experiment that grounds it, so the
two can be checked against each other; where the companion later re-cuts
them, the pin fixes which reading this profile adopted (P6, P3).

1. Effective blanket is geometric, not set-theoretic (exp 17). A boundary
   stated as attribute-column membership leaks under bypass. The
   load-bearing structure is the identity axis, and a set-valued boundary
   over columns is an epistemic convenience rather than the object. The
   Representation law (§8) is read this way: the test is whether identity
   survives treatment, not which attributes are in the member set.
2. Attribute schemas sense and fragment; they do not isolate. Any fixed
   attribute basis partially aligns with a given object's identity and
   partially distributes it. Where a Markov-object overlay is published,
   it exposes the identity axis, not only the attribute profile. Schemas
   are evidence, not ontology.
3. Core identity, not core size, is the discriminator of objecthood (exps
   15, 16). A sparse invariant with semantically loaded content is a
   lawful object; a rich attribute cluster with nothing invariant under
   context variation is not. More columns do not buy more objecthood.
   This is why sparse first publication remains lawful under the
   Saturation law (§11).
4. Identity is a DC shift, not a principal-variance axis (exp 18). Object
   identity appears as a mean offset in representation space, not as the
   dominant-variance direction. Characterisation by "the biggest source of
   variance in the attribute set" systematically misses identity;
   characterise by typical offset from a null peer instead. This is the
   basis for excluding principal-component and maximum-variance
   constructions as identity directions (§10).

These refinements do not weaken the construct; they sharpen it into one
that can be operationally validated and reproduced in published overlays.
They constrain the construct and overlays built on it. They are not
admissibility conditions for entity cuts, which §9 governs (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Candidate evidence supports the pinned working reading, not formal closure: exp17 favours a geometric identity axis and treatment survival over column membership; fixed schemas partly sense/distribute identity and published overlays expose the axis; exps15/16 distinguish invariant semantic identity from core size, permitting sparse identity but rejecting rich noninvariant clusters; exp18 identifies DC mean offset from null peers rather than principal variance, excluding PCA/maximum-variance identity extraction. Later companion recuts do not change the pinned reading.
constraints.uncertainty: The experiments themselves are not supplied or independently assessed.

exceptions: Entity cuts are judged by their own admissibility test and do not inherit Markov candidate status.

grounding.quote:
Adopting this profile does not
require that the empirical program be complete. Commitments that depend on
a formally established conditional-independence object, for example
claims that a published Markov-object overlay is the blanket rather than
a candidate for it, are read as working commitments, open to revision
when the companion program produces a conditional-independence result
(P6, P5).

Promotion gate. The experimental result that would promote the construct
from candidate to established is a direction-native
conditional-independence test: given the identity projection, residual
variation along remaining components should be independent of the target
under plausible treatments. That test has been run and did not meet its
predicate, and its multi-layer successor did not either. The gate stands
where it is; it has not been met and is not relocated to accommodate the
negative result (P6).

This status attaches to the construct and to overlays built on it. A
published Markov-object overlay is a candidate-class overlay of a
candidate construct, not a certified blanket of a formally established
object. It does not attach to entity cuts: an entity cut is lawful
published truth on its own admissibility test (§9) and does not inherit
the construct's candidate status. A candidate entity that has not met
that test is a candidate; a published entity cut is not (P3, P6). The
status is inherited downstream: tooling that materialises Markov-object
overlays under this profile should default to a candidate-class
publication kind and reserve any formally closed publication kind for
cuts backed by a real promotion-gate result (P6).

constraints.statement: Adoption does not require completed empirical research. Formal-blanket-dependent commitments remain revisable working commitments. Promotion requires a direction-native conditional-independence result: given identity projection, remaining-component residual variation should be independent of target under plausible treatment. Both the test and multi-layer successor failed their predicates; the unmet gate is not relocated. Tooling should default to candidate-class publication and reserve formal closure for actual promotion-gate evidence. Neither candidate standing nor a passed publication verification certifies a statistical blanket.
constraints.uncertainty: Empirical statements are retained as the profile's reports.

conditions: If a Markov object is read as a candidate identity-bearing cut.
exceptions: The empirical Markov program is not a prerequisite for all design work.

grounding.quote:
If a Markov object is read as a
candidate identity-bearing cut, good software boundary design should
prefer:

- the smallest lawful carrier set that preserves the boundary's real
  authority;
- subordinate payloads staying subordinate unless they carry independent
  authority;
- resistance to boundary inflation, where many sensed fragments are
  promoted into peer objects without irreducible need;
- strongly typed semantic boundaries, so identity-bearing cuts are not
  left fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned.

This profile does not make the empirical Markov-object program a
prerequisite for all design work. The relation runs the other way: this
profile gives one theoretical framing for why these boundary disciplines
are sound, and DESIGN_MODULE gives the general engineering law that
remains valid even outside world-model products (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Boundary design should prefer the smallest lawful authority-preserving carrier set, subordinate payloads unless independently authoritative, resistance to unnecessary peer-object inflation and strongly typed semantic boundaries. WORLD_MODEL supplies one theoretical account; DESIGN_MODULE owns general engineering law valid beyond world-model products.
constraints.uncertainty: The external design law is not reconstructed.

grounding.quote:
Mappings are semantic treatments. Cross-domain transformation is not
plain structural rewrite. Every treatment declares preserved structure,
changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity (P1, P4b;
rc.2 #mappings-are-semantic-treatments). A treatment is a refinement or
rewrite step of
[ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement): what it preserves
and its licensing law are that section's, and a treatment that changes
meaning is an approximate step with its adequacy relation. The five
declared fields are this profile's domain fields for that statement;
preserved structure is what the step preserves, and changed meaning,
loss, surplus and ambiguity state where and how it is not exact.

Fully qualified naming is mandatory. Many cross-domain failures are
preventable naming collisions. Fully qualified naming removes aliasing,
so the remaining hard work is real semantic transformation; IDENTITY §2
states the scoped identity it applies (P3, P1;
rc.2 #fully-qualified-naming-is-mandatory).

Value lists are domain artifacts too. Changing code sets,
classifications and value lists are governed temporal reference
artifacts, not static enum decorations (P3;
rc.2 #value-lists-are-domain-artifacts-too).

The world model sits above APIs and schemas. API contracts and schema
contracts are projections over the world model. They are useful because
they publish structure and function; they are not the highest semantic
authority (P6, P1; rc.2 #the-world-model-sits-above-apis-and-schemas).

Probability belongs in the epistemic overlay. The canonical published
entity cut should remain semantic and bounded. Probability belongs in
uncertainty, ranking, anomaly and alignment overlays, not in the
ontological identity of the published object itself (P3, P6;
rc.2 #probability-belongs-in-the-epistemic-overlay).

constraints.statement: Source systems retain operational truth; contextual data traces function and is invalid as isolated meaning; world models externalise expert understanding. Every treatment declares preservation, changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity. Meaning-changing treatment is approximate and carries its adequacy relation under external refinement/licensing law. Fully qualified naming is mandatory. Changing enumerations are governed temporal artifacts. API/schema contracts are subordinate projections. Published identity should remain semantic/bounded; probability belongs to epistemic overlays, not ontological identity.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION refinement licensing and adequacy definitions are external.

exceptions: Align, Compile and Serve/query are optional; compilation applies where real execution is needed, serving where delivery needs justify it.

grounding.quote:
2. Trace. Index and locate the source surfaces that may support semantic
   claims. Tracing should make it possible to point from a later
   world-model attribute claim back to the concrete source span, field,
   locator, code path or record that supports it.
3. Extract. Produce reviewable intermediate surfaces from traced source
   objects: source inventories; object candidates; event and lifecycle
   candidates; treatment candidates; authority candidates; ambiguity
   registers. These are not the world model yet; they are the auditable
   path toward it.
4. Assure. Qualify traced observations into lawful world-model claims.
   Assurance should make explicit what is being claimed; whether the
   claim is observed, derived, interpreted or composed; which source
   surfaces support it; which source is authoritative for which aspect of
   the claim; and what ambiguity or missingness remains.
5. Ledger. Write the accepted qualified claims into the attribute ledger.
   The ledger is append-only: new understanding is recorded as new
   qualified claims and later object cuts, not by mutating prior accepted
   entries in place.
6. Bound. Identify bounded contexts and the candidate entities that
   actually cohere inside them. Reject schema-first modelling and
   vocabulary-cluster modelling. Define local boundaries in terms of
   function, authority, state and adjacency.

11. Align (optional). Use the semantic kernel as a tether for
    probabilistic alignment across domains, entity cuts, artifacts and
    projections. This stage may produce correspondence candidates,
    confidence-ranked alignments, ambiguity overlays, mapping suggestions,
    and anomaly or mismatch overlays. These outputs are epistemic
    overlays, not yet published semantic truth.
12. Project. Emit familiar outputs from the same semantic kernel: tables;
    schema contracts; API contracts; event contracts; mapping documents;
    transformation specifications; covariant transforms; tests and
    application scaffolds where applicable.
13. Compile (optional). Where delivery requires real execution, compile
    accepted semantic understanding into deterministic executable
    artifacts. Examples may include data-movement specifications,
    transformation jobs, high-volume ETL or ELT plans, deterministic
    mapping-tool records and generated implementation artifacts. The
    important rule: probabilistic correspondence may help comprehension;
    accepted semantic understanding governs compilation; execution at
    scale should run through deterministic compiled artifacts rather than
    through row-by-row probabilistic inference (P0, P6).
14. Serve or query (optional). If delivery needs justify it, expose
    traversal or query capability over published domain artifacts and
    composed world models. This may remain filesystem-first in the
    low-volume lane or later move behind a dedicated query plane.

constraints.statement: Observe strongest available evidence. Trace should locate concrete source support. Extract auditable inventories/object/event/lifecycle/treatment/authority candidates and ambiguity registers, not yet the model. Assure should state claim, observed/derived/interpreted/composed kind, supporting source and aspect-specific authority, residual ambiguity/missingness. Append accepted claims without mutating prior entries. Bound by function/authority/state/adjacency, rejecting schema-first or vocabulary-cluster modelling. Materialise sufficiently contextual cuts, allowing bounded/distinguishable/evidenced sparse first publication. Relate through treatments/covariance/adjoints/temporal references. Publish immutable cuts with Git/filesystem sufficient at low volume. Compose recursively/inspectably/boundedly without erasing local authority. Optional alignment yields epistemic outputs only. Project tables, schema/API/event contracts, mapping documents, transformation specifications, covariant transforms, tests and applicable scaffolds. Optional compilation uses accepted understanding for deterministic artifacts, including movement specs/jobs/ETL/ELT/mapping-tool records/generated code; execution at scale should avoid rowwise probabilistic inference. Optional serving may remain filesystem-first or use a later query plane.
constraints.uncertainty: This is a descriptive encoding of stages, not an executed traversal.

conditions: Every published entity cut; geometric details only where a declared representation space exists.
exceptions: Outside a representation space, discharge the boundary law semantically under entity-cut construction.

grounding.quote:
Every published entity cut is prompt-sufficient for reasoning (P3, P1;
rc.2 #representation-law). At minimum, the cut should make visible
identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and
ambiguity. "Make the effective blanket explicit" means: state the
boundary at which the entity's identity survives reinterpretation, not
enumerate a set of member attribute columns. Attribute schemas are
evidence for identity, not identity itself. The boundary is
interventional, not structural: the test is "does this identity survive
treatment across its adjacent domains?", never "which attributes are in
the member set?" (P3). Where a declared representation space exists, that
boundary takes its geometric form, the low-rank projection along which
identity is preserved under treatment, and a Markov-object overlay should
then expose both the distributed attribute evidence and the projection
that recovers identity from it. Outside such a space the same law is
discharged semantically under §9 (P3, P1).

constraints.statement: Each published cut is prompt-sufficient for reasoning and should at minimum expose its eight semantic surfaces. Identity-survival under adjacent-domain treatment, not attribute membership, defines the interventional boundary. Schemas evidence identity rather than constitute it. In a declared space, an overlay should expose both distributed evidence and the low-rank identity-recovering projection.
constraints.uncertainty: Prompt-sufficiency has no independent operational test specified here beyond the stated surfaces and boundary law.

grounding.quote:
`source -> tracing -> assurance -> attribute ledger -> entity cut`

The entity cut is the immutable projection, not the mutable source of
truth. "Projection" is literal: the cut selects one bounded identity and
boundary over the distributed evidence in the ledger, accompanied by that
evidence and the basis on which it was accepted; §9 states the
obligation, and §10 applies where the selection is expressed
geometrically in a declared representation space (P3). The attribute
ledger is the accepted semantic record over which the entity cut is
projected. A single ledger state can support many different cuts at
different identities, boundaries and context scopes; the cut records
which selection was taken, not that the ledger is the cut (P3, P1).

Every accepted object attribute should therefore be recoverable through
the object cut that contains it; the attribute-ledger entries that
justify it; the assurance basis that accepted those entries; and the
traced source surfaces that support the assurance. No object attribute
should exist without ledger support; no ledger entry should exist without
assurance; no assurance should exist without traceable source (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: A materialised cut is the builder's canonical object-level semantic artifact, not a raw source emission or replacement operational truth. Published domain artifacts should be versioned and explicitly superseded. The chain is source→tracing→assurance→ledger→cut. A cut selects bounded identity/boundary with evidence and acceptance basis; one ledger state may support multiple identities/boundaries/context cuts. Every accepted attribute should be recoverable through cut, ledger, assurance and traced source; none should lack the next supporting link.

grounding.quote:
Published world-model truth should be immutable per cut; reviewable by
diff; traceable to evidence; and superseded by explicit later cuts rather
than silently overwritten (P4b, P3; rc.2 #publication-law). The
filesystem and Git are sufficient for the publication plane in the
initial lane. A database, if introduced later, is a query-plane
complement rather than the constitutional publication authority. In other
words: Git is the publication ledger; a database is the query plane
(P6). This publication ledger is distinct from the attribute ledger: the
attribute ledger records qualified semantic claims over object identity,
and the publication ledger records immutable published cuts of domain
artifacts and object projections. Both should remain append-only and
replayable (P4b).

constraints.statement: Published truth should be immutable per cut, diff-reviewable, evidence-traceable and explicitly superseded instead of silently overwritten. Publication and attribute ledgers remain distinct and both should be append-only/replayable. Git/filesystem suffice initially; a later database complements querying rather than replacing constitutional publication authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The should modality here coexists with explicit immutable-cut prohibitions in Flow, Publishing a cut and Overlay publication.

grounding.quote:
The attribute ledger is the immediate semantic source of an entity cut
(P4b, P6; rc.2 #attribute-ledger-law). Every entry should be a fully
qualified claim, potentially including a value or measured quantity; a
rule or constraint; a classification; a topology or relation claim;
provenance and authority information; and effective, observed and
publication coordinates. The ledger may be supported by one or more
evidence surfaces, including documents for declared semantics or policy,
code for derivation logic or invariants, and data for observed state or
emitted values. The profile does not assume one source per attribute; it
assumes one lawful claim record per accepted attribute fact (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: The ledger immediately sources entity-cut semantics. Each entry should be fully qualified, potentially carrying value/quantity, rule/constraint, classification, topology/relation, provenance/authority and effective/observed/publication coordinates. One or more sources may support it: documents for declared semantics/policy, code for derivation/invariants, data for state/values. Require one lawful claim record per accepted fact, not one source per attribute.

grounding.quote:
Entities are recovered, not invented. A builder project constructs an
entity cut by trawling authoritative source surfaces for the boundaries
the operating model already commits to, then qualifying them into
published truth (P3, P6; rc.2 #entity-cut-construction-law).

constraints.statement: Recover rather than invent entities: inspect authoritative source surfaces for boundaries already committed by the operating model and qualify those into published truth.

conditions: Publication of an entity cut.
exceptions: Sparse, unique, historical, single-context, inaccessible or regulated entities remain publishable when the test holds with declared residual ambiguity/evidence limits.

grounding.quote:
An entity cut is admissible when its identity, boundary, authority,
state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity are explicit,
traceable, and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence
altitude proportional to the claim (P3, P6; rc.2 #admissibility). That is
the whole constitutional test. It binds what is true of a published cut;
it does not prescribe how a builder establishes it (P0).

"Explicit" admits three lawful values on every surface: a stated value,
stated absence, or stated non-applicability with its reason. A cut whose
entity has no adjacent-domain treatment says so; it does not manufacture
one. This keeps the predicate whole without adding evidence machinery
(P5).

Sparse first publication remains lawful. A unique, historical,
single-context, inaccessible or regulated entity is publishable when the
test above holds and its residual ambiguity is declared. Absence of a
comparison population, of repeated contexts, or of permission to
intervene is a bound on evidence altitude to be stated, not a bar to
publication (P5, P2).

constraints.statement: The whole constitutional test requires all eight surfaces explicit, traceable and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence altitude proportional to the claim, without prescribing establishment technique. Every surface may state a value, absence, or non-applicability with reason; do not manufacture treatments. Missing comparison populations, repeated contexts or intervention permission are stated evidence-altitude bounds, not automatic publication bars.

conditions: Interventional evidence preference applies where the builder can intervene.
exceptions: No listed discrimination technique is mandatory or exhaustive.

grounding.quote:
"Discriminated from plausible alternatives" means the cut states why
this boundary rather than a nearby one the operating model would treat
differently. The claim carries its own discrimination; a stronger claim
needs stronger discrimination (P3, P6; rc.2 #discrimination). Techniques
that serve this, none of them mandatory and none of them exhaustive:

- cross-context invariance: separate what holds wherever the entity
  appears from what a particular context adds, where multiple contexts
  exist;
- null-peer comparison: name a structurally similar entity the operating
  model treats differently, and state what separates them;
- adjoint round-trip: interpret the entity through an adjacent domain's
  treatment surface and back through its adjoint mapping, and show the
  identity claim survives;
- transplant: show what a neighbouring entity would have to acquire to be
  treated as this one;
- coat stripping: vary or remove contextual claims and show identity
  survives; vary an identity claim and show it does not.

The adjoint round-trip performs, at semantic altitude, the discrimination
the geometric boundary test performs in a representation space. Where a
builder can intervene, interventional evidence discriminates more
strongly than declarative evidence, and a cut should say which kind it
rests on (P6). Boundary is interventional in character, not structural.
A cut that states its boundary only as a set of source fields has made a
weaker claim than one that states the reinterpretations under which
identity survives, and should be read as such (P3, P1).

constraints.statement: State why this boundary rather than a nearby differently treated alternative; stronger claims need stronger discrimination. Optional techniques are multiple-context invariance, structurally similar null peers, identity-preserving adjoint round-trip, transplant prerequisites and coat stripping versus identity-claim variation. Semantic adjoint round-trip corresponds to geometric boundary testing. Interventions discriminate more strongly where possible; cuts should identify evidence kind. A source-field-only boundary is a weaker claim than treatment-survival and should be read accordingly.

conditions: A cut is published or its identity/boundary revised.

grounding.quote:
A published entity cut makes the eight admissibility surfaces (identity,
boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and
ambiguity) visible and traceable, each as a stated value, stated absence
or stated non-applicability, and records the basis on which identity was
discriminated (P3, P6; rc.2 #publication). Cuts are immutable: revising
identity or boundary produces a new cut that supersedes the prior one
(P4b). Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology are
consumer realisation; this profile requires that the published surfaces
survive and does not select the form they are stored in (P0, P2).

constraints.statement: Publish all eight visible/traceable surfaces with their lawful value modes and the identity-discrimination basis. Cuts are immutable; identity or boundary revision creates a superseding cut. Consumer-chosen storage form must preserve the published surfaces.

conditions: Only where a builder operates in a declared learned representation, ledger embedding or equivalent metric space in which identity is geometric.
exceptions: Ordinary institutional recovery does not require this overlay law.

grounding.quote:
This law is the representation-substrate specialisation of §9. It
applies only where the builder operates over a declared representation
space in which identity is a geometric direction (a learned
representation, an embedding over ledger claims, or an equivalent metric
space); it is not required for ordinary institutional recovery (P3, P2;
rc.2 #markov-object-construction-law). Where it applies, a builder
project constructs the overlay by a directional, interventional
procedure. The steps below are both how the overlay is built and the
minimum structure that is stored when it is published. The declared
representation space is part of the overlay: an identity direction is
uninterpretable without the space it lives in, and directions computed in
different spaces do not compose (P3, P1).

constraints.statement: Use the directional/interventional construction procedure and retain its minimum published structure. The declared representation space is part of the overlay; a direction without its space is uninterpretable and directions from different spaces do not compose.

conditions: Constructing a geometric overlay for a candidate object.

grounding.quote:
For a candidate object, assemble attribute-ledger evidence across context
variation together with evidence for at least one null peer (P3, P6;
rc.2 #1-paired-evidence-collection):

- multiple contexts in which the candidate is instantiated;
- a null-peer instance: a structurally similar thing that lacks the
  candidate's identity content, observed in the same contexts;
- paired ledger entries covering `(candidate, context)` and
  `(null, context)`, so identity-carrying signal can be separated from
  context-carrying signal.

The paired evidence is the raw material of the cut. The ledger entries
remain distributed; they are not the object (P3).

constraints.statement: Collect multiple candidate contexts and at least one structurally similar identity-lacking null peer observed in the same contexts; pair candidate/context and null/context ledger entries to separate identity from context signal. Distributed ledger evidence is raw material, not the object itself.

conditions: Accepting a candidate direction or publishing its overlay.
exceptions: A lawful underlying entity cut remains publishable without the overlay.

grounding.quote:
A candidate identity direction is accepted only if projection along it
preserves object identity under held-out treatments. The builder records
at least one acceptable verification (P6, P3;
rc.2 #3-verification-by-treatment):

- α-sweep: apply `x − α · d` on held-out contexts, and show the expected
  identity shift and its saturation behaviour;
- transplant: apply `x + α · d` to null-peer instances, and show identity
  acquisition;
- boundary test: overwrite attributes outside the projection support and
  show identity survives (this is what discriminates a geometric blanket
  from a set-membership blanket).

A direction that has no acceptable verification is a candidate, not an
accepted overlay. Publishing an unverified direction violates the
Representation law (§8). The underlying entity cut remains lawful and
publishable without the overlay (P6, P3). The empirical program that
motivates these treatments reports that the strongest of them,
direction-native conditional independence, has been tested and does not
close. Passing this battery establishes that a direction is verified for
publication under this profile; it does not establish a formally closed
Markov blanket (§4 Epistemic status) (P6).

constraints.statement: Acceptance requires held-out treatment preservation and at least one recorded acceptable verification: α-sweep x−α·d with expected shift/saturation; transplant x+α·d into null peers showing acquisition; or outside-support overwrite preserving identity. Without acceptable verification the direction stays candidate and publication violates Representation law. Passing verifies publication fitness, not formal Markov closure; the reported conditional-independence test did not close.

conditions: Candidates appear in multiple contexts.

grounding.quote:
For candidates that appear in multiple contexts, decompose the attribute
evidence into an invariant core, the attributes whose contribution to the
identity direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts, and a context
coat, the attributes selected by the specific context, carrying
contextual reinterpretation rather than identity per se (P3;
rc.2 #4-core-and-coat-decomposition). Both are evidence. The core carries
identity; the coat carries treatment. The coat to core ratio is a
characterisation, not a quality metric (P3, P1).

constraints.statement: Decompose evidence into identity-stable invariant core across ≥ N of N contexts and context-selected treatment coat. Keep both as evidence and do not use coat/core ratio as a quality metric.
constraints.uncertainty: N and the quantitative meaning of stable are not further specified in this section.

conditions: Before publication of the accepted Markov-object representation.
exceptions: Core size overlapping null-peer ranges is expected and acceptable; size is not diagnostic.

grounding.quote:
Before publication, discriminate an accepted Markov object from an
incidental attribute cluster by null-peer comparison (P3, P6;
rc.2 #5-null-peer-discrimination):

- is the candidate's core size in a range that null peers also hit? Yes
  is expected and acceptable; size is not diagnostic;
- are the identity-loaded attributes in the core unique to the candidate
  among its null peers? They should be;
- does the candidate's identity direction transfer more cleanly than a
  random diagonal in the representation? It should.

Failure on the uniqueness and transfer tests means the cluster is not yet
a lawful Markov object, even if its invariants are internally consistent
(P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Perform null-peer discrimination. Identity-loaded core attributes should be unique among null peers and direction transfer should be cleaner than a random diagonal. The result mapping later makes either failed uniqueness or failed transfer a not-yet-lawful result, even with internally consistent invariants; overlapping core size alone is acceptable.
constraints.uncertainty: The source does not quantify uniqueness tolerances or cleaner transfer.

conditions: An overlay is published or revised.
exceptions: Effective α coordinate is required where applicable.
constraints.statement: Expose at minimum versioned space/attribute basis, geometric direction, ledger-traced core/coat evidence, verification treatments/outcomes/held-out contexts, support where identity survived, null-peer tested/accepted/rejected comparisons, and applicable α. Overlays are immutable: revised directions/new evidence/contexts/refitted space create superseding overlays. Space change supersedes all expressed directions even if ledger entries are unchanged; never mutate prior overlays.

conditions: Storing a Markov-object overlay.
constraints.statement: Store a package attached to its entity cut, not a table-row or membership-list substitute. Retain all six surfaces: versioned space; direction/support; ledger evidence pointers; treatment/context/outcome verification trace; accepting actor/assurance provenance and authority; supersession predecessor if any. Loss of any surface makes storage unlawful. Query/projection conveniences do not substitute.

exceptions: Sparse first publication remains lawful under admissibility.

grounding.quote:
World-model construction is iterative. Builder projects may work a
bounded source-object set repeatedly until the resulting attribute ledger
is judged sufficiently saturated for publication (P2, P5;
rc.2 #saturation-law). Sufficient saturation means: materially important
attributes have traceable support; remaining gaps are explicit
ambiguities rather than silent misses; and the resulting object cut is
stable enough to publish and supersede later if needed. Sparse first
publication remains lawful (§9 Admissibility); silent unsupported
attribute creation does not (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Builders may iterate over a bounded source-object set until judged sufficiently saturated. Sufficiency means traceable materially important attributes, explicit remaining ambiguities rather than silent misses, and a cut stable enough to publish/supersede. Silent unsupported attribute creation is unlawful.
constraints.uncertainty: No numerical saturation threshold is specified.

exceptions: Detailed mesh topology may remain product-local while the line develops.

grounding.quote:
Do not build one central monolith first. Build local published domain
artifacts and their entity cuts, then stitch them (P4a, P6;
rc.2 #composition-law). Composition preserves fragment authority,
bounded-context meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and
ambiguity. Higher-order models are composed from published domain
artifacts; they do not erase them (P4a, P4b). The preferred end state is
a federated world-model mesh rather than a single flattened enterprise
model. Detailed mesh topology may remain product-local while the line is
still being developed; profile-level mesh law should be ratified only
once the reusable node and edge model is stable (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Build local published artifacts/cuts before stitching, not a central monolith first. Preserve fragment authority, bounded-context meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and ambiguity; higher-order models do not erase constituents. Prefer a federated mesh; profile mesh law should be ratified only after reusable node/edge structure stabilises.
constraints.uncertainty: Mesh law/topology remains developing and product-local.

conditions: Temporal-reference traceability applies where applicable.

grounding.quote:
Projection is downstream convenience, not semantic authority; the
semantic kernel remains primary (P6, P1; rc.2 #projection-law). All
projections should remain traceable back to governing objects; evidence;
treatments; covariance edges; adjoint mappings; and temporal reference
artifacts where applicable. Tables, schemas, APIs, mapping documents and
covariant transforms are all publication forms over the same semantic
kernel (P1). Because an API usually carries more business semantics than
a bare schema, the preferred structural order is
`world model -> API contract -> schema contract`. Query and traversal are
also downstream-facing conveniences in this sense: they may be a
first-class delivery pillar without becoming the constitutional core of
this profile (P6, P2).

constraints.statement: Keep the semantic kernel primary; projections are conveniences, not semantic authority. All should trace to governing objects, evidence, treatments, covariance, adjoints and applicable temporal references. Tables/schemas/APIs/mapping documents/covariant transforms share that kernel. Prefer world model→API contract→schema contract because APIs usually carry more business semantics. Query/traversal may be first-class delivery without becoming constitutional core.

conditions: Large-scale movement where semantic understanding is accepted and compilable.

grounding.quote:
LLMs and other probabilistic systems belong primarily on the semantic
control plane. They should help with comprehension, candidate alignment,
ambiguity reduction and correspondence ranking. They should not be the
row-by-row execution engine for large-scale data movement when the
semantic understanding has already been accepted and can be compiled
(P0, P2).

constraints.statement: Probabilistic systems primarily serve semantic control and should help comprehension, candidate alignment, ambiguity reduction and ranking. Under the stated conditions they should not serve as row-by-row bulk execution engines.

conditions: Compilation demonstration is recommended where the line is sufficiently mature.

grounding.quote:
Adoption should not depend on winning the standardisation argument first
(P2; rc.2 #proof-law). Preferred wedge:

1. comprehend one bounded source slice;
2. publish one fragment;
3. stitch one adjacent fragment;
4. answer one painful question the incumbent pipeline cannot answer
   cleanly;
5. emit both conventional and covariant outputs side by side.

This is incremental semantic capture, not a demand for immediate central
convergence. The proof obligation is practical: build the world model
once, then show that the same semantic substrate can emit the legacy
artifacts the organisation expects and the richer covariant outputs the
profile makes possible. Where the line is mature enough, the proof should
also show that accepted semantic understanding can be compiled into
deterministic executable pipelines without losing the traceability and
challengeability of the governing world model (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Adoption should not wait for a won standardisation debate. Prefer a five-step wedge: comprehend one bounded slice, publish one fragment, stitch one neighbour, answer one difficult incumbent question, emit conventional/covariant outputs together. The practical obligation demonstrates both legacy and richer outputs from one built semantic substrate, without demanding immediate central convergence. Mature lines should additionally demonstrate deterministic compilation retaining traceability and challengeability.

conditions: Choose normative application specifications for primarily interaction/workflow/non-domain/extra-domain operational-policy problems; choose world-model substrate for interfaces mainly over stable domain reality.
exceptions: Simpler lines may use world model→application projections→implementation.

grounding.quote:
The profile stands in parallel with spec-driven development.
Specifications are usually normative; world models are usually
descriptive. A sufficiently well-formed world model can therefore project
large parts of an application surface without requiring duplicated
semantic re-authoring downstream (P2, P1;
rc.2 #world-model-driven-development). Preferred relationship:

`world model -> epistemic correspondence overlay -> deterministic compiled artifacts -> implementation`

For simpler lines the shorter compression still holds:
`world model -> application projections -> implementation`. Use
normative application specs where the problem is primarily user
interaction, workflow choice, non-domain behaviour, or operational policy
beyond the domain semantics themselves. Use the world model as the
semantic substrate wherever the software is mainly an interface over
stable domain reality (P2, P1).

constraints.statement: World-model-driven and spec-driven development stand in parallel; specifications are usually normative and models usually descriptive. A sufficiently formed model can project large application portions without semantic reauthoring. Prefer world model→epistemic correspondence overlay→deterministic compiled artifacts→implementation, with the stated simpler alternative and problem-dependent use of normative specifications.

conditions: The source describes outputs expected if the profile is working.
exceptions: Markov overlays apply where a representation space is selected; compiled executables apply where real-volume safe movement is needed.
constraints.statement: Expected outputs comprise durable published domain artifacts, composed models, primary entity cuts, applicable inspectable Markov overlays, explicit treatments/covariance, grounded epistemic correspondence, temporal enumerations, familiar projections, applicable deterministic executables and a basis for institutional AI reasoning. This output inventory is not a result assigned to any actual product.

conditions: Cut admissibility is evaluated at the cut's claimed evidence altitude.
exceptions: Declared absence/non-applicability with reason is a lawful surface value, not a nonsatisfied result.

grounding.quote:
| cut admissibility | `cut_admissible` | satisfied | each surface is a stated value, a stated absence or a stated non-applicability with its reason, is traced, and is discriminated at the stated altitude; a stated bound on evidence altitude with its residual ambiguity declared meets the test (sparse first publication) |
| cut admissibility | `cut_inadmissible` | falsified | a surface is neither a stated value, a stated absence nor a stated non-applicability, or is untraceable, or the admissible evidence shows the boundary undiscriminated from a plausible alternative; that surface or alternative is the counterexample |
| cut admissibility | `discrimination_undecided` | indeterminate | no counterexample of `cut_inadmissible` is found, and the admissible evidence cannot decide the discrimination the cut itself claims at its stated altitude; the value names the evidence that would decide |

constraints.statement: cut_admissible→satisfied requires each surface lawful/traceable/discriminated, including sparse publication with stated altitude bound and residual ambiguity. cut_inadmissible→falsified identifies a missing/untraceable surface or evidenced undiscriminated plausible alternative. discrimination_undecided→indeterminate requires no inadmissibility counterexample and insufficient admissible evidence for the claimed discrimination; name deciding evidence.

conditions: Direction acceptance is evaluated.
exceptions: Unrun verification is handled separately and is not automatically indeterminate.

grounding.quote:
| direction acceptance | `direction_verified` | satisfied | the direction is built by an admissible extraction in its declared representation space, at least one acceptable verification is recorded with identity preserved under held-out treatment, and no recorded verification shows identity lost |
| direction acceptance | `extraction_inadmissible` | falsified | the direction is built by a principal-component or maximum-variance construction, which is not admissible as an identity direction, whatever its verification shows; that construction is the counterexample |
| direction acceptance | `verification_failed` | falsified | the extraction is admissible, and a recorded verification shows identity not preserved under held-out treatment; that verification is the counterexample |
| direction acceptance | `verification_inconclusive` | indeterminate | the extraction is admissible in a declared representation space, no recorded verification establishes an acceptable preservation or shows identity lost, and a recorded verification ran without establishing either; the value names the held-out treatment or verification that would decide |
| direction acceptance | `representation_space_invalid` | invalid_basis | no counterexample of `extraction_inadmissible` or `verification_failed` is found, and the overlay declares no representation space, or its direction is composed with directions computed in another space; that basis cannot support the evaluation (§10) |

constraints.statement: direction_verified→satisfied requires admissible extraction in declared space, at least one acceptable recorded held-out preservation and no recorded identity loss. extraction_inadmissible→falsified for PCA/maximum-variance regardless of verification. verification_failed→falsified for admissible extraction with recorded held-out identity loss. verification_inconclusive→indeterminate requires admissible extraction/declared space, a run establishing neither preservation nor loss and no other decisive recorded verification; name deciding treatment/test. representation_space_invalid→invalid_basis requires no extraction/verification counterexample and either no declared space or cross-space composition.

conditions: Each mapping concerns its own predicate.

grounding.quote:
| overlay publication | `published_verified` | satisfied | the published direction has a recorded acceptable verification |
| overlay publication | `published_unverified` | falsified | a direction with no acceptable verification is published, which violates §8 Representation law (§10 Verification by treatment); that publication is the counterexample |
| overlay storage | `storage_retained` | satisfied | the stored package retains the declared representation space and its version, the geometric object, the distributed evidence, the verification trace, the provenance and authority record, and the supersession record |
| overlay storage | `storage_lossy` | falsified | the stored layout loses one of those surfaces; the lost surface is the counterexample |
| null-peer discrimination | `null_peer_discriminated` | satisfied | the identity-loaded attributes in the candidate's core are unique to it among its null peers, and its identity direction transfers more cleanly than a random diagonal |
| null-peer discrimination | `not_yet_lawful` | falsified | the uniqueness test or the transfer test fails, so the cluster is not yet a lawful Markov object; the failing test is the counterexample |
| promotion gate | `gate_met` | satisfied | the run meets the test's predicate |
| promotion gate | `gate_not_met` | falsified | the run does not meet the test's predicate; it is the counterexample for that run only, and the construct's standing is unchanged |
| saturation | `saturated` | satisfied | the three conditions hold; the explicit gaps are carried as residuals |
| saturation | `not_saturated` | falsified | a condition fails, as where an attribute exists without traceable support (silent unsupported attribute creation) or a gap is a silent miss; that attribute or gap is the counterexample |

constraints.statement: published_verified→satisfied for recorded acceptable verification; published_unverified→falsified names publication without it. storage_retained→satisfied for all six package surfaces; storage_lossy→falsified names a lost surface. null_peer_discriminated→satisfied requires unique identity-loaded core and cleaner-than-random-diagonal transfer; either test failing yields not_yet_lawful→falsified with that test. gate_met→satisfied and gate_not_met→falsified concern only the test run; failed run leaves construct standing unchanged. saturated→satisfied requires all three support/gap/stability conditions and carries explicit gaps as residuals; not_saturated→falsified names a failed condition, unsupported attribute or silent gap.

conditions: Fallback applies when no refined value applies; the unrun case assumes no extraction_inadmissible or representation_space_invalid ground.

grounding.quote:
Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value
directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):
`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,
naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim
needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and
`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground
other than `representation_space_invalid` (P5).

A verification not run. Where no ground of `extraction_inadmissible` or
`representation_space_invalid` holds, a candidate direction whose
verification has not been run has no result for direction acceptance:
the verification is the evaluation of that predicate, and it was not
performed, so it has no
closed result and is never mapped to
`indeterminate` or to any other core value
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed). The
direction stays a candidate (§10 Verification by treatment). In every
conjunction over its acceptance, the unrun verification is a planned
assessment without a closed result
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Gaps) where the verification was planned; where none was planned, the
obligation it would have discharged is uncovered coverage. A step whose output needed that verification and that stopped
without it ends `incomplete`, which
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
maps for the predicate "a candidate is available", never to
`indeterminate`; the step's work state carries the unrun verification as
a residual ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)).
Publishing the unverified direction is `published_unverified` (P5, P6).

Two readings keep the mapping total without coercion (P5, P1). A stated
absence or stated non-applicability on an admissibility surface is a
lawful surface value, not a non-satisfied result. Candidate-class and
established are standings of the construct, the first being FOUNDATIONS
§5's hypothesis standing, and candidate-class and formally closed are
publication kinds; none of them is a result, and a gate run that fails
does not falsify the construct.

constraints.statement: Fallback indeterminate names deciding evidence; out_of_frame concerns needed undeclared relation/capability; invalid_basis concerns unsupported basis other than representation_space_invalid. An unrun verification, absent the specified prior invalidity grounds, gives no direction-acceptance result at all, never indeterminate or another core value, and leaves the direction candidate. Planned-but-unrun is a conjunction gap; unplanned is uncovered coverage. A dependent construction step stopping without it ends incomplete for the distinct candidate-availability predicate and carries the unrun test as work-state residual. Publishing it is nevertheless published_unverified. Lawful absent/inapplicable surface values, construct standings and publication kinds are not evaluation results; failed gate runs do not falsify the construct.
constraints.uncertainty: The external mapping of construction incomplete is not supplied and is not invented.

proof: a Msg log plus the final State and an empty Cmd sequence (P2).

forbidden: Changing the State → ViewTree contract or introducing side effects merely because a framework uses another implementation shape.

grounding.quote:
Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function
component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived
expression or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision
recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function
signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body
(P1, P0).

allowed: Per-project adoption limited to some UX surfaces, such as production UI excluding internal debug tools, with design-module scope recorded.

grounding.quote:
Adoption is per project. A project may adopt this profile only for some
UX surfaces, for example the production UI but not internal debug tools,
with the scope recorded in the design module (P2, P6).

allowed: Under the short-window cost condition: screenshot/walkthrough capture, visual review, copy/spacing/density/layout cleanup, accessibility review/remediation, meaningful-family replay-proof updates, design wording cleanup and trace cleanup between changed states and authority.
forbidden: Escrowing carrierless product-truth Msgs; new/changed typed product contracts; product-meaning-changing navigation/information architecture/selection authority; runtime/governance/closure/continuation/lineage/provenance/evidence semantics; release criteria or method law.

allowed: Stated value, stated absence or stated non-applicability with reason on each of eight surfaces.
Sparse first publication with adequate discrimination, declared evidence bounds and residual ambiguity; no required comparison population, repeated contexts or intervention permission.
forbidden: Manufacturing an adjacent-domain treatment where the entity has none.

grounding.quote:
"Explicit" admits three lawful values on every surface: a stated value,
stated absence, or stated non-applicability with its reason. A cut whose
entity has no adjacent-domain treatment says so; it does not manufacture
one. This keeps the predicate whole without adding evidence machinery
(P5).

Sparse first publication remains lawful. A unique, historical,
single-context, inaccessible or regulated entity is publishable when the
test above holds and its residual ambiguity is declared. Absence of a
comparison population, of repeated contexts, or of permission to
intervene is a bound on evidence altitude to be stated, not a bar to
publication (P5, P2).

allowed: Consumer choice of concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology, provided required published surfaces survive.
forbidden: In-place revision of published identity/boundary instead of a new superseding cut.

grounding.quote:
Cuts are immutable: revising
identity or boundary produces a new cut that supersedes the prior one
(P4b). Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology are
consumer realisation; this profile requires that the published surfaces
survive and does not select the form they are stored in (P0, P2).

allowed: Supervised linear-discriminant, logistic-regression-normal or difference-in-conditional-means variants when they target mean offset rather than within-class variance.
forbidden: Principal-component or maximum-variance constructions as identity directions.
Treating the direction as one attribute column rather than a geometric combination.

grounding.quote:
taken across contexts. Supervised variants (linear discriminant,
logistic-regression normal, difference-in-conditional-means) are
admissible when they target mean offset rather than within-class
variance. Principal-component and maximum-variance constructions are not
admissible as identity directions: they capture within-pair variation,
not the identity offset. The identity direction is not an attribute
column; it is a geometric combination over columns (P3).

limitations: This is source interpretation only: no semantic acceptance, installed qualification, product evaluation, execution or completeness judgment is asserted.

The schema has no active judgments, traversals or transformations populations. Source-defined evaluations, stage order, formulae and procedures are retained descriptively; no operational proof objects or runtime are instantiated.
Four heading-only sections are deliberately omitted as containers; their supplied child sections are interpreted.

The pinned empirical program was not supplied. Its findings, failed promotion-gate reports and standing are represented as source claims, not independent empirical verification.

Several named units and result domains are grouped in local concepts for compactness; their distinct meanings and predicates are retained in definitions and constraints. Matching labels across documents do not establish identity.
Foundation table premises, policy owners and consumer routes are retained as authored descriptions. No proof of those derivations or verification of their external consumers is claimed.
N/context stability, quantitative transfer quality, evidence-altitude calibration and saturation thresholds are not numerically fixed by these sections.
The supplied calculus basis is treated as the selected basis identifier only; subject references to a_c, ledgers, cuts, projections and result algebras do not redefine or execute that calculus.

conditions: The product publishes typed asset surfaces under its carrier law/design.
exceptions: Use the design-named equivalent contract when no AssetSurface contracts are published.

grounding.quote:
When the product publishes typed asset surfaces under the graph-execution
profile's carrier law and the local product's design, a UX surface binds
to one or more AssetSurface contracts as its data source and action
target (P6, P3; rc.2 #7-assetsurface-binding-rule). Binding requirements:

relations.meaning: The surface consumes data and targets actions through one or more admitted typed contracts subject to the binding law.

conditions: World-model publication under this profile, with adjacent-domain treatment as admissible change.

grounding.quote:
where FOUNDATIONS §2 defines an Object as
a subject with scoped identity, a boundary, current state and declared
material relations, and P3 makes a boundary a claim with a proof
obligation, a world-model builder binds them to the published entity cut
of §6 and its admissibility test of §9. Direction: profile to tier 1;
preserved meaning: identity is declared and survives admissible change,
and the boundary carries its own proof; narrowed scope: world-model
publication under this profile, where admissible change is treatment
across adjacent domains; invalidation: a change of §9 or of FOUNDATIONS
§2 Object or P3 re-evaluates the binding (P3, P1).

relations.meaning: Entity-cut publication/admissibility binds the described tier-1 Object and boundary-proof claims while preserving identity and proof meaning; specified input changes require reevaluation.

conditions: Selected complete method basis; exact four listed identities only.
exceptions: Changes to either context, cited concept/taxonomy clause or basis invalidate until reevaluated.

grounding.quote:
The meanings are adopted unchanged for this profile's scope under the
selected complete method basis. Their owner in FOUNDATIONS §2 is
retained, and a change to either context, any cited concept or taxonomy
clause, or the selected method basis invalidates the import until it is
reevaluated. The GLOSSARY only locates those source-owned meanings. No
other same-spelled concept is imported by this declaration. For each
import the source and target concept reference is the same listed
